title: Question: what is the current AI toolbox for UE5 and what can AI do in UE5
author: TrismegistusCinnabar
selftext:
I want to make a game in UE5.

It will take a lot of time and many give up.

I'm looking for ways to use AI to save time. What are the current tools you use?

For example: The total amout of time going to debugging code is probably a lot. Just having

AI tools for debugging C++ code in UE5 would be a huge time savior.

comments.author: lostforever2011
comments.body:
I am also interested in this... i want to make multiplayer RPG.

I have been trying to create 3d model and the import to UE5.8 and apply that mesh to UE5 manny using Claude fable. It kind of did it but it looks horrible when the animations run!

I know nothing about 3d but from what I understand fabled, took the 3d mesh and did some stuff in Blender and then some stuff in unreal. All headless and me giving visual feed back. Took good 3 to 4 hours but still not happy with it.  There are so many issue deformed hands and legs when running etc.

replies.author: TrismegistusCinnabar
replies.body: Did you create the 3D model in Blender?

replies.author: lostforever2011
replies.body: no, it was AI created model from text prompt.

replies.author: TrismegistusCinnabar
replies.body: I know almost nothing about 3D modelling in EU5, apart from that there are things that the engine don't translate very well, like when a 3D animation stretches itself

replies.author: lostforever2011
replies.body: I am programmer and no nothing about art, 3d or animation as well! I am wondering if I am over my head with UNreal even with fable!

replies.author: TrismegistusCinnabar
replies.body: Does it not come back to the difference between panning and executing? If we cannot divide the task in to doable parts, we end up saying it is "too hard" or "too much"
